rules.sentence: The Brugada pattern is to be differentiated from Brugada syndrome.

Patients can present to the ED in one of three scenarios: After resuscitation from sudden cardiac death with subsequent ECG demonstrating the Brugada pattern; after an episode of syncope or palpitations with the Brugada pattern noted on the ECG; and incidentally without symptoms of malignant dysrhythmia and the pattern noted on the ECG.

The electrocardiographic presentation of the Brugada pattern can easily be misinterpreted as a STEMI with the presence of ST-segment elevations in right precordial leads; in fact, the ST-segment elevation has been described as a STEMI mimic.
The most frequent ECG findings in the Brugada pattern include incomplete (or complete) RBBB and ST-segment elevation in leads V1 and V2.
